question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in execute-on-parse mode for core agent-loop tool scheduling, and must it wait for explicit concurrency-safety metadata such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62962?
rationale: The source-level latency opportunity is clear, but the change alters core runtime semantics, safety policy, hook timing, transcript ordering, and likely config/API surface rather than repairing a narrow existing contract.

options.title: Design opt-in core mode
options.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner design covering eligibility, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and regression proof before implementation.

options.title: Block on tool safety metadata
options.body: Treat execute-on-parse as dependent on a separate concurrency-safety contract such as the open tool classification issue before any early execution can start.

options.title: Defer runtime semantics change
options.body: Leave current post-stream parallel batching as the only supported behavior if maintainers judge early execution too risky for now.

recommendation.title: Design opt-in core mode
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner design covering eligibility, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and regression proof before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent history ties steipete to the central agent-core and provider-stream surfaces that would need the design decision.
